title: Invocation signal aggregator & regression harness for function-selection and arg-integrity
creator: Kira Novak
description: Build a reusable eval harness that aggregates per-request invocation signals (selection score, top-k margin, schema-conformance, argument type conformance, token-length drift) and surfaces regression alerts when config or model changes reduce tool selection accuracy or argument integrity. Focus on: 1) a compact signal model that can run in CI/canary without full eval reruns, 2) scenario-based fuzz tests for edge-case arguments, 3) calibration of a 'selection confidence' metric tied to downstream correctness, and 4) integration with Console alerts/dashboards and canary rollouts.
tasks: Design the invocation signal schema and lightweight scorer (selection_confidence, arg_valid_score, schema_violation_count)
Implement ingesters for live telemetry and offline replay (support prefix-KV priming and cached responses)
Add scenario-based fuzzbench generator for common tool patterns (date parsing, numeric ranges, file paths, structured JSON payloads)
Create CI job that runs signal aggregator on canary model/config changes and emits regression verdict
Wire alerts to Console with drilldowns to example requests and failing cases
Author runbook for triaging selection vs argument failures and promote to rollback policy
acceptance_criteria: Signal aggregator produces stable per-request metrics for 95% of requests in both realtime and replay modes
Canary CI job flags regressions when selection_accuracy drops >3% on curated scenario set
Arg-validation detects schema violations with >90% precision on held-out fuzzbench
Console dashboard shows time-series of selection_confidence and arg_valid_score per model variant and exposes sample requests for each alert
Documented runbook and at least one cross-team review approval recorded
